title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA1RF_1LD0LE_1RE0RA_1LC0RD_0RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA1RF_1LD0LE_1RE0RA_1LC0RD_0RE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is pairs 10 / 01 cut by markers 11, plus a reservoir of the word 1010101 at the left end. Nearly all segments are frozen copies of a few shapes, grouped in levels of growing size. The run of pairs at the right end of the frozen part shrinks at a steady rate while the reservoir grows. The crossings of the pairs are proved in Lean. What happens when the last run is used up (a new level?) is not worked out, so halting (F reading a 1) is not ruled out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,332 cells have been visited and 32,786 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: linear/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 1.01). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462).

claims.title: Crossing pairs
claims.text: D> (01)^n → (10)^n D>, E> (10)^n → (01)^n E>, (01)^n E> 0 → E> 0 (01)^n, (10)^n C> 1 → C> 1 (10)^n, for every n.

claims.title: Frozen levels and a steady drain
claims.text: At the left-end records at steps 838,623,265, 911,286,865 and 987,150,465 the tape is C> (01)^4 (1010101)^r (01)^7, then 9 segments (10)^11 11 (01)^43, then 6 segments (10)^83 11 (01)^403, then larger ones ((10)^162 11 (01)^893, (10)^565 11 (01)^893 twice, (10)^6 11 (01)^1162), and a final run (01)^m. Only r and m change: r = 5,323, 5,723, 6,123 and m = 4,323, 3,923, 3,523.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when F reads a 1. F is entered from B on a 1 (writing 1, moving right). In the steady phase above, the drain repeats the same moves. But the final run will be used up after about 9 more such samples, and what follows (likely a new level of segments) is not worked out. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: D, E and C crossing runs of pairs.
No halt in the C simulator; 66,332 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Frozen levels
html: Everything between the reservoir (1010101)^r and the last run (01)^m is identical in the samples at 8.4·108, 9.1·108 and 9.9·108 steps. Segment sizes grow from level to level (43, 403, then about 900 and more), which suggests that each level was built when the previous drain ran out.

sections.heading: Draining the last run
html:
Between samples, 400 pairs of the last run disappear (4,323, 3,923, 3,523) and 400 copies of 1010101 join the reservoir (5,323, 5,723, 6,123). The tape grows by 2,000 cells to the left. The head crosses runs of pairs in one go (proved in Lean) and carries the material across the frozen levels.

What halting would need. F reading a 1. The steady drain makes the same moves each time, so a halt could only come at a transition, such as when the last run is empty and a new level has to be built. The next step is to run until that happens (about 109 more steps) and record the transition as a rule.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 1.01). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,332 cells (10,417 left of the start, 42,071 right), with a density of 1s of 0.494.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A hierarchy of frozen segments (10)^a 11 (01)^b whose sizes grow level by level (43, 403, 893, …); the active end eats the last run of pairs 01 at a steady rate, 400 pairs per sample, and turns it into a growing reservoir of the word 1010101 at the far left.
family: bouncer feeding a reservoir, with nested frozen levels
